title: Çatalhöyük
summary: Çatalhöyük is a pair of settlement mounds on the Konya Plain in central Turkey. The east mound has 18 Neolithic levels dated 7400–6200 BCE and the west mound Chalcolithic levels to 5200 BCE. Its densely packed houses entered by roof and its wall paintings make it a key site for early settled farming. UNESCO inscribed it in 2012.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives rounded BCE spans for the east tell (7,400–6,200 BC) and west tell (6,200–5,200 BC); the project site says only that the settlement dates back 9000 years.

as_recorded.value: east tell 7,400-6,200 BC; west tell 6,200-5,200 BC

where.modern_name: Çatalhöyük, Çumra district, Konya Province, Türkiye
where.historical_name: No polity; Neolithic and Chalcolithic settlement on the Konya Plain, central Anatolia

importance.justification: One of the best-preserved early farming settlements, central to understanding the rise of sedentary life and symbolic culture.

sources.title: The Site, Çatalhöyük Research Project
sources.publisher: Çatalhöyük Research Project (Stanford University, British Institute at Ankara and partners)

reviewer_note: Least sure of the end date: UNESCO runs occupation to 5200 BCE via the west mound, while the east mound is abandoned about 6200 BCE; other scholarship gives somewhat different spans.
